name: Terraria: TShock
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Terraria with TShock, the server mod with accounts, permissions and plugins. The world is created on first start.
startup: if [ -x ./TShock.Server ]; then DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major exec ./TShock.Server -ip 0.0.0.0 -port {{SERVER_PORT}} -maxplayers {{MAX_PLAYERS}} -world {{WORLD_NAME}}.wld -autocreate {{WORLD_SIZE}}; elif command -v mono >/dev/null; then exec mono TerrariaServer.exe -ip 0.0.0.0 -port {{SERVER_PORT}} -maxplayers {{MAX_PLAYERS}} -world {{WORLD_NAME}}.wld -autocreate {{WORLD_SIZE}}; else echo "TShock 4 runs with Mono: choose the Mono image in Startup, then start the server again."; exit 1; fi

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Terraria: TShock. Downloads a TShock release from GitHub, checked against
# GitHub's checksum. Worlds, configs and plugins are never touched; TShock's
# files are replaced only once the new ones are downloaded and unpacked.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server

repo=Pryaxis/TShock
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
build=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
trap 'rm -rf "$build"' EXIT

want="${TSHOCK_VERSION:-latest}"
if [ "$want" = latest ]; then
    tag=$(gh-release tag "$repo") || fail "GitHub can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."
else
    case "$want" in v*) ;; *) want="v$want" ;; esac
    tag=$(gh-release tag "$repo" "$want" 2>/dev/null) ||
        fail "TShock has no version $want. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as $(gh-release tag "$repo" 2>/dev/null || echo v6.2.1)."
fi
assets=$(gh-release assets "$repo" "$tag") || fail "GitHub can't be reached right now. Reinstall to try again."

case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) pattern='linux-(x64|amd64)' ;;
    aarch64) pattern='linux-arm64' ;;
    *) fail "TShock has no build for this CPU." ;;
esac
asset=$(awk '{print $1}' <<<"$assets" | grep -E "$pattern" | grep -E '\.zip$' | head -n1 || true)
if [ -z "$asset" ]; then
    # TShock 4 is one zip for every CPU, run with Mono.
    asset=$(awk '{print $1}' <<<"$assets" | grep -viE 'win|osx|linux|mac' | grep -E '\.zip$' | head -n1 || true)
fi
[ -n "$asset" ] || fail "TShock $tag has no download for this CPU (Linux $(uname -m))."
sum=$(awk -v a="$asset" '$1 == a { print $2 }' <<<"$assets")

if [ -n "$sum" ] && [ "$sum" != - ] && [ "$(cat .raptor-version 2>/dev/null)" = "$tag $sum" ]; then
    echo "TShock $tag is already installed."
else
    mkdir -p "$build/x"
    echo "Downloading TShock $tag ($asset)"
    gh-release download "$repo" "$tag" "$asset" "$build/tshock.zip" || fail "The download failed. Reinstall to try again."
    unzip -q -o "$build/tshock.zip" -d "$build/x"
    for t in "$build"/x/*.tar; do
        [ -e "$t" ] || continue
        tar -xf "$t" -C "$build/x" && rm -f "$t"
    done
    # Some releases put everything in one folder.
    src="$build/x"
    if [ "$(find "$src" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 | wc -l)" = 1 ] && [ -d "$(find "$src" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)" ]; then
        src=$(find "$src" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
    fi
    # Files the last release had and this one doesn't (another version's
    # libraries) are removed; nothing else is.
    (cd "$src" && find . -type f | sort) > "$build/files"
    if [ -f .raptor-files ]; then
        comm -23 <(sort .raptor-files) "$build/files" | while read -r f; do rm -f -- "$f"; rmdir -p --ignore-fail-on-non-empty "$(dirname "$f")" 2>/dev/null || true; done
    fi
    cp -a "$src/." .
    mv -f "$build/files" .raptor-files
    if [ -f "$src/TShock.Server" ]; then rm -f TerrariaServer.exe; else rm -f TShock.Server TShock.Installer; fi
    chmod +x TShock.Server TShock.Installer 2>/dev/null || true
    echo "$tag $sum" > .raptor-version
fi
if [ -f TShock.Server ]; then
    echo "Installed TShock $tag."
else
    echo "Installed TShock $tag. It runs with Mono: choose the Mono image in Startup."
fi

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The TShock release, such as v6.2.1, or latest for the newest one. TShock 4 needs the Mono image. Reinstall the server after changing it.

variables.name: World name
variables.description: The world file to run, without .wld. It's created when it doesn't exist.

variables.name: World size
variables.description: The size of a new world: 1 small, 2 medium, 3 large.

variables.name: Max players
variables.description: The most players that can be online at once.
